posts.body_html:
A gangsta rapper who also happened to be a thug once said, "I may be slippin, but never trippin." With regards to S. Vitner's Treasure, I'm not sure if I'm trippin or not....cuz I'm a plant nerd, not gangster: do we seriously not have a thread on Phillup Fulleasy-E's (that a ridiculous spelling for Phil Faulisi) masterpiece, S. Vitner's Treasure?! I couldn't find one, maybe there's one already made.

Well, I haven't had this plant for a very long time, so can't say too much about it other than it's easy to grow, produces beautiful, colorful traps both during the spring and fall, and it's pretty dang good looking overall! Correct me if I'm wrong, but this is supposedly a sibling to S. "Tyranna" aka S. Saurus, right?

Feel free to add pics or any of your experience with this clone here! I'm just getting the topic started here.

Pic taken 5/27/20:


Edit: I just looked at the pic and noticed that red throated moorei in the background photo-bombing the F out of this shot! It's like that moorei has it's mouth open with amazement, LOL

posts.body_html:
I believe Vintner's Treasure is from the amazing moorei cross seed pod Phil made between leuco purple lips and his breeder ornata. The single seed pod I think is responsible for VT, Saurus, Hot Lips, Super Heavy Veins and many more amazing Moorei! Just goes to show what knowing the genetics of your parent plants can do for producing amazing offspring. Hopefully one day I'll get to that level! Still a lot left to learn

I'm not fortunate enough to grow VT yet, but I do grow Super Heavy Veins, Hot Lips and Phil Clone 7 and they are all among the nicest plants in my collection. To answer hungry_plants 's question - it looks like VT is named after Phil's favorite Paph. orchid hybrid. Taken from the cultivar description here:

legacy.carnivorousplants.org/cpn/Species/v42n4p145_152.html#vitner
